paper.title_en: Scaling of soft QGP signatures in relativistic lead, xenon, and oxygen collisions in EPOS4
paper.abstract_en: The collective expansion and hydrodynamic evolution in heavy-ion collisions is well established. However, whether femtometer-scale droplets of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) are produced in small systems at high energies remains a fundamental open question. Analysis of Pb-Pb collisions at <math><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt></math> = 5.02 TeV, Xe-Xe collisions at <math><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt></math> = 5.44 TeV, and O-O collisions at <math><msqrt><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></msqrt></math> = 5.36 TeV using EPOS4 is reported to make predictions and postdictions. The results are compared with ALICE data for Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions. Charged particle multiplicity <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>ch</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>η</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> and transverse-momentum <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> spectra for pions <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, kaons <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, and protons <math><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>p</mi><mspace width="0.28em"/><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></math> are studied. The inclusion of a hadronic afterburner, UrQMD (Ultrarelativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics) is found to be necessary to correctly describe baryon yields. <math><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math> fluctuations are also studied via normalized <math><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math> correlator, <math><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo>〈</mo><mrow><mo>〈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>〉</mo></mrow><mo>〉</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>〈</mo><mrow><mo>〈</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub><mo>〉</mo></mrow><mo>〉</mo></mrow></mrow></math>. Lastly, anisotropic flow harmonics <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> <math><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo>{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> are computed as a function of <math><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msub></math> and centrality. Since EPOS4 has not been extensively studied for flow observables, this study thereby provides a nontrivial assessment of its collective dynamics. The results are compared with experiment wherever data are available. Taken together, this study provides a unified description of soft observables from Pb-Pb through Xe-Xe down to O-O and offers quantitative guidance on how such collisions may inform of the properties of the QGP.
